# Short walkthroughs and selected reading

Each original walkthrough has four short text segments, a full transcript, and a pause before your own response. The portal presents one segment at a time. Reading a transcript is a complete route; no audio, video, or particular learning style is required.

Use a walkthrough when a concept blocks your next attempt. Its examples use hiking, libraries, recipes, document extraction, and research instead of solving the assigned Signal Desk exercise. A provisional 5–10 minutes per walkthrough allows reading and short pauses; record your own actual time.

## Selected external reading

The following section names were checked on the official pages on 20 October 2026. They are reading targets, not claims that you completed the source. Pages can change; use the title if a section moves. No video timestamps are invented.

- **After the first diagram:** in [Anthropic's Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents), read “What are agents?” and “When (and when not) to use agents.” Write one case where a fixed workflow meets your contract. This is a conceptual article originally published in 2024; the page itself notes later changes in tooling.
- **After your first packet:** in [Anthropic's Effective context engineering](https://www.anthropic.com/research/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents), read “The anatomy of effective context” and “Context retrieval and agentic search.” Return to your own packet and remove one irrelevant item while preserving its decisive exception.
- **Before the Python component labs:** in [the official Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/), select dictionaries, defining functions, modules, reading/writing files, and errors/exceptions. It assumes basic programming knowledge; if programming itself is new, use the beginner worksheet with a tutor and reserve further preparation time.

The academy's existing resource library contains the longer courses and video links. Choose one that answers a problem you encountered, record the selected section title and one resulting experiment, and return to your own project. Watching more material is not a substitute for a reviewed attempt.
